messages:
Sean Gallagher: Hey all — we’ve published the first *canonical* Tiered SLO definitions (Hosted vs Dedicated) + the Error Budget Policy & enforcement plan. This is the “source of truth” going forward for how we measure reliability and what happens operationally when we burn budget.

Links:
• Tiered SLO definitions (Hosted vs Dedicated): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGSRE/Tiered+SLO+definitions+%28Hosted+vs+Dedicated%29
• Error budget policy + enforcement (burn rates, actions, exceptions): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGSRE/Error+budget+policy+and+enforcement
• SLI spec (success/timeouts/streaming disconnect taxonomy): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGSRE/SLI+spec+-+success%2C+timeouts%2C+streaming+disconnects
• Runbook (what to do when near/exhausted): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ONCALL/Error+budget+exhaustion+response+runbook

What’s new / what changes for teams:
1) We now have tier-specific SLOs for key journeys (chat/completions streaming + non-streaming, embeddings, and Dedicated pool readiness).
2) Error budget burn is the leading indicator; we’ll start “feeling” burn via rollout gates + progressive delivery constraints (initially warn-only).
3) Definitions include explicit exclusions (invalid auth, customer-side disconnects/timeouts where attributable, misuse).

Rollout plan (high level):
• Next 1–2 weeks: dashboards + burn alerts wired for the initial set of services (gateway + routing + control plane)
• Enforcement: warn-only first, then soft-block in pilot once we’re confident in SLI correctness

Huge thanks to @Rafael Mendes @Aisha Bello @Allison Grant @Sergio Costa and partners across Platform + Product. :tada:
(reactions: :tada: x18, :thumbsup: x31)

Rafael Mendes: Adding one important callout: please *don’t* copy/paste old “availability” queries into new dashboards. Use the SLI definitions from the spec page. We already found a couple cases where 499/timeout attribution differs between nginx logs vs metrics.

Aisha Bello: If you own a service on the request path (gateway -> routing -> runtime) and you’re not seeing `tier` consistently in metrics yet, ping me or @Nadia Rahman. We’re tracking gaps + backfills and don’t want teams building custom label hacks.

Priya Natarajan: +1. This is also the dependency for rollout gating we’re building into deploy tooling. If we have inconsistent tier propagation, gates will be noisy (or worse, incorrect).

Marissa Cole: From Product side: this is also what we’ll surface in Console (budget remaining + burn) and tie into Rollouts UX. If you have feedback on what’s “actionable” vs just “interesting”, drop it here or DM me/@Chloe Martin.

Lauren Bishop: Dedicated-specific note: the Dedicated SLO table includes the pool readiness SLI. That’s intentionally separate from request success rate. For Dedicated customers, readiness dips are often *the* early warning before request errors show up.

Ethan Park: Quick clarification on enforcement timeline — are we doing warn-only gates for *all* services or only the pilot set?

Sean Gallagher: Only pilot set first (gateway + routing + control plane deploys). We’ll publish the exact list once the dashboards + burn alerts are stable. Goal is no surprises / no “random blocks” because of early SLI bugs.

Sahana Iyer: For folks asking about the gate mechanics: if your pipeline is onboarded, you’ll see a new step that posts a “Budget check: OK/WARN/BLOCKED” comment. In warn-only mode it will never block the deploy.
We’ll post a short how-to once the first repos are enabled.

Miles Thornton: Also worth noting: the runbook has the mitigation order we want oncall to follow (fallback routing, protective throttling for Hosted, feature flag rollback). We’re trying to reduce the “everyone does a different thing” problem.

Allison Grant: PSA: burn-rate alerting uses multi-window burn (fast + slow) to avoid flapping. If you’re defining new alerts for your service, please align to the org standard here: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ARCH/Error+budget+burn-rate+alerting+standard

Dev Patel: Support/CS angle: if you’re in an incident and see a budget burn spike, please follow the comms triggers in the runbook. We’ve had a bunch of “should we post status?” ambiguity — this is meant to remove that.

Wei Chen: Q on exclusions: if a customer sets an aggressively low client timeout (e.g. 2s) and we see disconnects, is that excluded from Hosted SLO?

Aisha Bello: If we can attribute it as client abort (gateway sees client close before first byte / before headers, etc.), it’s excluded from *server-side* availability. But streaming disconnects are trickier — that’s why the disconnect taxonomy page exists. If you have a concrete example, drop request IDs in #eng-sre and we’ll sanity-check.

Sergio Costa: Dashboards are landing in the standard folders this week. Naming convention doc here (WIP but usable): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGPLAT/SLO+dashboards+structure+and+naming

Chloe Martin: If you want Console visibility on these (esp Dedicated customer-facing views), we’re collecting requirements on permissions + filtering (tier/region/model/route). Send notes; we’re trying to avoid building something only SREs can interpret.

Priya Natarajan: Thanks everyone. Last request: if you see incorrect burn calculations / mismatched error counts, file it early. We’d rather fix measurement now than debate policy exceptions later.
(reactions: :thumbsup: x22)
